correctness.rationale: Orient the link so that successive outward triangles have vertex order (v,u_i,u_{i+1}). Their boundary labels are (radial_i, external_i, radial_{i+1}); hence radial labels advance by the same nonzero step modulo three. Closing the link gives 3|q, and every three sectors use each included angle exactly once, giving qπ/3. A genuine extreme vertex of the full-dimensional convex polytope has positive angular defect, forcing q=3. Euler and 3V=2E=3F give V=4, and two edges of a given scalene length cannot be incident, so they are opposite. For necessity of the box form, translate the tetrahedral centroid to zero and write the four vertex vectors as x+y+z, x−y−z, −x+y−z, −x−y+z, with x,y,z the three independent Hadamard half-sum directions. Opposite-edge equality gives y·z=z·x=x·y=0 by subtracting the squared norms of the corresponding sum and difference. Full dimension makes all three squared coordinate lengths positive, exactly the three strict acute inequalities. The converse has axis half-turns preserving outward orientation and transitive on facets. Right triangles give a zero direction, obtuse triangles a negative required squared length. The proof does not rely on the supporting finite examples or on artificial coplanar subdivisions.
